import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils.dataframe import dataframe_to_rows

# Read the initial workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Read Sheet1 data using pandas
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Extract Product column and sort in ascending order
products = df['Product'].sort_values(ascending=True).reset_index(drop=True)

# Create a new dataframe with just the Product column
product_df = pd.DataFrame({'Product': products})

# Remove 'Products' sheet if it already exists
if 'Products' in wb.sheetnames:
    del wb['Products']

# Create a new sheet for sorted products
ws = wb.create_sheet('Products')

# Write the sorted product data to the new sheet (with header)
for r_idx, row in enumerate(dataframe_to_rows(product_df, index=False, header=True), 1):
    for c_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws.cell(row=r_idx, column=c_idx, value=value)

# Save the workbook to output.xlsx
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import LineChart, Reference
from openpyxl.chart.label import DataLabelList

# Read the initial workbook
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Profit column
df['Profit'] = df['Sales'] - df['COGS']

# Save to a temporary file first with pandas
df.to_excel('./temp_output.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1', index=False)

# Load with openpyxl to add chart
wb = load_workbook('./temp_output.xlsx')
ws = wb.active

# Create a line chart
chart = LineChart()
chart.title = "Weekly Sales, COGS, and Profit Trend"
chart.style = 13
chart.y_axis.title = "Amount"
chart.x_axis.title = "Week"
chart.legend.position = "b"  # Legend at bottom

# Determine the data range
# Headers are in row 1, data starts from row 2
num_rows = len(df) + 1  # +1 for header row

# Sales data (column B)
sales_data = Reference(ws, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_col=2, max_row=num_rows)
chart.add_data(sales_data, titles_from_data=True)

# COGS data (column C)
cogs_data = Reference(ws, min_col=3, min_row=1, max_col=3, max_row=num_rows)
chart.add_data(cogs_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Profit data (column D)
profit_data = Reference(ws, min_col=4, min_row=1, max_col=4, max_row=num_rows)
chart.add_data(profit_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Set the categories (Week column)
cats = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=num_rows)
chart.set_categories(cats)

# Add chart to worksheet
ws.add_chart(chart, "E2")

# Save the final workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

# Clean up temp file
import os
os.remove('./temp_output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import AreaChart, Reference

# Read the input workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Read data into pandas for easier manipulation
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Filter for GDP indicator - handle potential variations in naming
gdp_df = df[df['IndicatorName'].str.contains('Gross Domestic Product', case=False, na=False)].copy()

# Get year columns (all columns except Country and IndicatorName)
all_cols = df.columns.tolist()
year_cols = [col for col in all_cols if col not in ['Country', 'IndicatorName']]
year_cols_numeric = sorted([int(col) for col in year_cols if str(col).isdigit()])
year_cols_filtered = [str(y) for y in year_cols_numeric if y >= 2003]

# Keep only Country, IndicatorName, and years from 2003 onwards
cols_to_keep = ['Country', 'IndicatorName'] + year_cols_filtered
gdp_df = gdp_df[cols_to_keep].copy()

# Convert year columns to numeric
for col in year_cols_filtered:
    gdp_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(gdp_df[col], errors='coerce')

# Find top 10 countries by 2013 GDP (or latest available year if 2013 not present)
if '2013' in gdp_df.columns:
    target_year = '2013'
else:
    target_year = year_cols_filtered[-1] if year_cols_filtered else None

if target_year:
    top10_countries = gdp_df.nlargest(10, target_year)['Country'].tolist()
else:
    top10_countries = gdp_df.nlargest(10, year_cols_filtered[0])['Country'].tolist() if year_cols_filtered else []

# Create a new sheet for the breakdown
if 'GDP_Breakdown' in wb.sheetnames:
    del wb['GDP_Breakdown']
ws_new = wb.create_sheet('GDP_Breakdown')

# Write headers
headers = cols_to_keep
for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers, start=1):
    ws_new.cell(row=1, column=col_idx, value=header)

# Write data
for row_idx, (_, row) in enumerate(gdp_df.iterrows(), start=2):
    for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers, start=1):
        value = row[header]
        ws_new.cell(row=row_idx, column=col_idx, value=value)

# Create stacked area chart for top 10 countries
# Filter data for top 10 countries
chart_df = gdp_df[gdp_df['Country'].isin(top10_countries)].copy()
chart_df = chart_df.sort_values(by=target_year, ascending=False)

# Prepare data for chart: rows are countries, columns are years
chart_data_rows = len(chart_df)
chart_data_cols = len(year_cols_filtered)

# Create the area chart
chart = AreaChart()
chart.title = "Top 10 GDP"
chart.style = 13
chart.grouping = "stacked"

# Set up references
# Data starts at row 2, column 3 (first year column after Country and IndicatorName)
# Countries are in rows 2 to (2 + chart_data_rows - 1)
# Years are in columns 3 to (3 + chart_data_cols - 1)

# Add series for each year
for i, year in enumerate(year_cols_filtered):
    col_num = 3 + i  # Column C is 3, D is 4, etc.
    # Reference: (min_row, min_col, max_row, max_col)
    values = Reference(ws_new, min_row=2, max_row=chart_data_rows + 1, min_col=col_num, max_col=col_num)
    categories = Reference(ws_new, min_row=2, max_row=chart_data_rows + 1, min_col=1)
    chart.add_series(values, titles_from_data=False, title=year)

# Set categories (country names)
chart.set_categories(categories)

# Position legend on the right
chart.legend.position = 'r'

# Add chart to worksheet
ws_new.add_chart(chart, "I2")

# Save the output workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook

# Read the input workbook
df_transactions = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')
df_pricing = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Pricing Table')

# Function to find price based on number of rolls
def get_price(num_rolls, pricing_df):
    num_rolls = int(num_rolls)
    for _, row in pricing_df.iterrows():
        units_from = int(row['Units From'])
        units_to = int(row['Units To'])
        if units_from <= num_rolls <= units_to:
            return row['Price per Roll (100 feet)']
    # If no range matches, return None
    return None

# Apply price lookup
df_transactions['Price'] = df_transactions['Number of Rolls'].apply(lambda x: get_price(x, df_pricing))

# Calculate revenue
df_transactions['Revenue'] = df_transactions['Number of Rolls'] * df_transactions['Price']

# Load workbook with openpyxl to preserve all sheets
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Update Price (column C, index 3) and Revenue (column D, index 4) columns
# Data starts from row 2 (row 1 is header)
for idx, row in df_transactions.iterrows():

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import BarChart, Reference

# Read the input workbook
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Create pivot table - sum of revenue by product
pivot = df.groupby('Product')['Revenue ($)'].sum().reset_index()
pivot = pivot.sort_values('Revenue ($)', ascending=False)
pivot.columns = ['Product', 'Total Revenue']

# Load the workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Create a new sheet for the pivot table
ws = wb.create_sheet('Product Revenue')

# Write headers
ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value='Product')
ws.cell(row=1, column=2, value='Total Revenue')

# Write the pivot table data
for r_idx, row in enumerate(pivot.values, 2):
    for c_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws.cell(row=r_idx, column=c_idx, value=value)

# Create a horizontal bar chart
chart = BarChart()
chart.type = "bar"
chart.orientation = "bar"  # Horizontal bars

# Set up data references (data is in column 2, categories in column 1)
data = Reference(ws, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_row=len(pivot)+1)
cats = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=len(pivot)+1)

chart.add_data(data, titles_from_data=True)
chart.set_categories(cats)

# Set chart title
chart.title = "Revenue of each product"

# Turn off legend
chart.legend = None

# Position the chart (anchor to cell D2)
ws.add_chart(chart, "D2")

# Save the output workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.styles import numbers

# Read the input workbook
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Present Value using the formula:
# PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n*t)
# Where r = Annual Interest Rate, n = # Compound Periods, t = Years, FV = Future Value

def calculate_present_value(row):
    fv = row['Future Value']
    rate = row['Annual Interest Rate']
    n = row['# Compound Periods']
    years = row['Years']
    
    pv = fv / ((1 + rate / n) ** (years * n))
    return pv

df['Present Value'] = df.apply(calculate_present_value, axis=1)

# Write to output using openpyxl to preserve formatting
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Write the calculated present values to column B (Present Value)
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    # Excel rows are 1-indexed, and we have a header row
    excel_row = idx + 2  # +2 because idx is 0-based and row 1 is header
    
    # Write the present value
    pv_value = row['Present Value']
    ws.cell(row=excel_row, column=2, value=pv_value)
    
    # Set accounting number format for Present Value column
    ws.cell(row=excel_row, column=2).number_format = '_($* #,##0.00_);_($* (#,##0.00);_($* "-"??_);_(@_)'

# Load the workbook
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb.active

# Check if the sheet name is Sheet1, if not, get the first sheet
if 'Sheet1' in wb.sheetnames:
    ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Get the number of rows and columns
max_row = ws.max_row
max_col = ws.max_column

# Based on the schema:
# Column A (1): Year
# Column B (2): Current Assets
# Column C (3): Fixed Assets
# Column D (4): Other Assets
# Column E (5): Assets (to calculate)
# Column F (6): Current Liabilities
# Column G (7): Long-term Liabilities
# Column H (8): Owner's Equity
# Column I (9): Liabilities & Owner's Equity (to calculate)

# First, check if column I exists, if not we may need to add the header
# Check the header row (row 1)
header_row = 1

# Find column indices by reading headers
col_map = {}
for col in range(1, max_col + 1):
    cell_value = ws.cell(row=header_row, column=col).value
    if cell_value:
        col_map[str(cell_value).strip()] = col

# Column indices (1-based)
col_year = col_map.get('Year', 1)
col_current_assets = col_map.get('Current Assets', 2)
col_fixed_assets = col_map.get('Fixed Assets', 3)
col_other_assets = col_map.get('Other Assets', 4)
col_assets = col_map.get('Assets', 5)
col_current_liabilities = col_map.get('Current Liabilities', 6)
col_longterm_liabilities = col_map.get('Long-term Liabilities', 7)
col_owner_equity = col_map.get("Owner's Equity", 8)

# Check if Liabilities & Owner's Equity column exists
col_liabilities_equity = col_map.get("Liabilities & Owner's Equity", None)

# If it doesn't exist, add it as column 9
if col_liabilities_equity is None:
    col_liabilities_equity = 9
    ws.cell(row=header_row, column=col_liabilities_equity).value = "Liabilities & Owner's Equity"

# Accounting number format
accounting_format = '_($* #,##0.00_);_($* (#,##0.00);_($* "-"??_);_(@_)'

# Process data rows (skip header row)
for row in range(header_row + 1, max_row + 1):
    # Get values for Assets calculation
    current_assets = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_current_assets).value
    fixed_assets = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_fixed_assets).value
    other_assets = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_other_assets).value
    
    # Convert to numbers if they're strings
    try:
        current_assets = float(current_assets) if current_assets else 0
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        current_assets = 0
    
    try:
        fixed_assets = float(fixed_assets) if fixed_assets else 0
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        fixed_assets = 0
    
    try:
        other_assets = float(other_assets) if other_assets else 0
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        other_assets = 0
    
    # Calculate Assets
    assets = current_assets + fixed_assets + other_assets
    ws.cell(row=row, column=col_assets).value = assets
    ws.cell(row=row, column=col_assets).number_format = accounting_format
    
    # Get values for Liabilities & Owner's Equity calculation
    current_liabilities = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_current_liabilities).value
    longterm_liabilities = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_longterm_liabilities).value
    owner_equity = ws.cell(row=row, column=col_owner_equity).value

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils.dataframe import dataframe_to_rows

# Read the initial workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Read data into pandas for calculation
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Present Value using the formula:
# PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n*t)
# Where: FV = Future Value, r = Annual Interest Rate, n = # Compound Periods, t = Years
df['Present Value'] = df['Future Value'] / (1 + df['Annual Interest Rate'] / df['# Compound Periods']) ** (df['Years'] * df['# Compound Periods'])

# Round to 2 decimal places for currency
df['Present Value'] = df['Present Value'].round(2)

# Update Sheet1 with calculated Present Values (column B, starting from row 2)
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    ws.cell(row=idx + 2, column=2, value=row['Present Value'])

# Create new sheet with No., Present Value, Future Value
new_df = df[['No.', 'Present Value', 'Future Value']].copy()

# Create the new sheet
wb.create_sheet('Investment Summary')
ws_new = wb['Investment Summary']

# Write headers and data to new sheet
for r_idx, row in enumerate(dataframe_to_rows(new_df, index=False, header=True), 1):
    for c_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws_new.cell(row=r_idx, column=c_idx, value=value)

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

expenses_col = headers.index('Total Expenses Before Tax') + 1
profit_col = headers.index('Profit Before Tax') + 1

        # Apply Currency format to Profit Before Tax
        ws.cell(row=row, column=profit_col).number_format = '"$"#,##0.00'

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.styles import PatternFill

# Read the workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Read data into pandas for calculations
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Gross Profit = Net Sales - COGS
df['Gross Profit'] = df['Net Sales'] - df['COGS']

# Calculate Operating Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses
df['Operating Profit'] = df['Gross Profit'] - df['Operating Expenses']

# Calculate Net Profit = Operating Profit - Tax Expense
df['Net Profit'] = df['Operating Profit'] - df['Tax Expense']

# Calculate Net Profit Margin = Net Profit / Net Sales
df['Net Profit Margin'] = df['Net Profit'] / df['Net Sales']

# Find the row with highest Net Profit Margin (in the dataframe)
max_margin_idx = df['Net Profit Margin'].idxmax()

# Update the workbook with calculated values
# Column mapping: Year=1, Net Sales=2, COGS=3, Gross Profit=4, 
#                 Operating Expenses=5, Operating Profit=6, Tax Expense=7, Net Profit=8
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    row_num = idx + 2  # Excel rows start at 1, header is at row 1, data starts at row 2
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=4).value = row['Gross Profit']
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=6).value = row['Operating Profit']
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=8).value = row['Net Profit']

# Add new column header for Net Profit Margin at column 9
ws.cell(row=1, column=9).value = 'Net Profit Margin'

# Add Net Profit Margin values
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    row_num = idx + 2
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=9).value = row['Net Profit Margin']

# Apply red fill to the cell with highest Net Profit Margin
red_fill = PatternFill(start_color='FF0000', end_color='FF0000', fill_type='solid')
max_margin_row = max_margin_idx + 2  # Convert dataframe index to Excel row
ws.cell(row=max_margin_row, column=9).fill = red_fill

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils.dataframe import dataframe_to_rows

df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Gross Profit = Net Sales - COGS
df['Gross Profit'] = df['Net Sales'] - df['COGS']

# Operating Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses
df['Operating Profit'] = df['Gross Profit'] - df['Operating Expenses']

# Net Profit = Operating Profit - Tax Expense
df['Net Profit'] = df['Operating Profit'] - df['Tax Expense']

# Load the workbook to preserve existing sheets
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Update Sheet1 with calculated values
ws1 = wb['Sheet1']

# Write calculated values back to Sheet1 (starting from row 2, skipping header)
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    excel_row = idx + 2  # Excel rows start at 1, header is row 1, data starts at row 2
    # Column D = Gross Profit (index 3)
    ws1.cell(row=excel_row, column=4, value=row['Gross Profit'])
    # Column F = Operating Profit (index 5)
    ws1.cell(row=excel_row, column=6, value=row['Operating Profit'])
    # Column H = Net Profit (index 7)
    ws1.cell(row=excel_row, column=8, value=row['Net Profit'])

# Create pivot table: Total Operating Expenses by Year
pivot_df = df.groupby('Year', as_index=False)['Operating Expenses'].sum()
pivot_df.columns = ['Year', 'Total Operating Expenses']

# Create a new sheet for the pivot table
if 'Pivot Table' in wb.sheetnames:
    del wb['Pivot Table']

# Add headers

ws_pivot.cell(row=2, column=2, value='Total Operating Expenses')

    excel_row = idx + 3  # Start at row 3 (after title and headers)
    ws_pivot.cell(row=excel_row, column=1, value=row['Year'])

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import LineChart, Reference

# Read the initial workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Get the data range (row 1 is headers)
max_row = ws.max_row

# Tax rate
tax_rate = 0.225

# Fill in columns D (Profit Before Tax) and E (Tax Expense)
for row in range(2, max_row + 1):
    sales = ws.cell(row=row, column=2).value
    expenses = ws.cell(row=row, column=3).value
    
    if sales is not None and expenses is not None:
        # Convert to numeric if they're strings
        try:
            sales = float(sales)
            expenses = float(expenses)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
        
        profit_before_tax = sales - expenses
        tax_expense = profit_before_tax * tax_rate
        
        ws.cell(row=row, column=4).value = profit_before_tax
        ws.cell(row=row, column=5).value = tax_expense

# Create line chart
chart = LineChart()
chart.title = "Sales and Profit Before Tax"
chart.style = 10
chart.y_axis.title = "Amount"
chart.x_axis.title = "Week"
chart.legend.position = "b"  # bottom

# Add Sales series (column B)
sales_data = Reference(ws, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_col=2, max_row=max_row)
chart.add_data(sales_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Add Profit Before Tax series (column D)
profit_data = Reference(ws, min_col=4, min_row=1, max_col=4, max_row=max_row)
chart.add_data(profit_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Set categories (Week column A, excluding header)
cats = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=max_row)
chart.set_categories(cats)

# Position the chart starting at cell G2
ws.add_chart(chart, "G2")

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import LineChart, Reference

# Load the workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb.active

# Tax rate
tax_rate = 0.225

# Find the last row with data
last_row = ws.max_row

# Fill in columns D (Profit Before Tax) and E (Tax Expense)
for row in range(2, last_row + 1):
    sales = ws.cell(row=row, column=2).value  # Column B - Sales
    expenses = ws.cell(row=row, column=3).value  # Column C - Total Expenses Before Tax
    
    if sales is not None and expenses is not None:
        # Convert to float if string
        try:
            sales = float(sales)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            sales = 0
        try:
            expenses = float(expenses)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            expenses = 0
        
        profit_before_tax = sales - expenses
        tax_expense = profit_before_tax * tax_rate
        
        ws.cell(row=row, column=4).value = profit_before_tax  # Column D
        ws.cell(row=row, column=5).value = tax_expense  # Column E

# Create a line chart
chart = LineChart()
chart.title = "Sales and Profit Before Tax"
chart.style = 10
chart.y_axis.title = "Amount"
chart.x_axis.title = "Week"
chart.legend.position = "b"  # bottom

# Data for Sales (Column B) - include header row for series name
sales_data = Reference(ws, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_row=last_row, max_col=2)
chart.add_data(sales_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Data for Profit Before Tax (Column D) - include header row for series name
profit_data = Reference(ws, min_col=4, min_row=1, max_row=last_row, max_col=4)
chart.add_data(profit_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Categories (Week column - Column A, starting from row 2 to skip header)
cats = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=last_row)
chart.set_categories(cats)

# Add chart to worksheet starting at cell G2
ws.add_chart(chart, "G2")

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import LineChart, Reference

# Read the input workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Read data using pandas for easier manipulation
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Profit Before Tax and Tax Expense
tax_rate = 0.225
df['Profit Before Tax'] = df['Sales'] - df['Total Expenses Before Tax']
df['Tax Expense'] = df['Profit Before Tax'] * tax_rate

# Write the calculated values back to the worksheet (columns D and E)
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    row_num = idx + 2  # Excel row number (1-indexed, +1 for header row)
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=4, value=row['Profit Before Tax'])
    ws.cell(row=row_num, column=5, value=row['Tax Expense'])

# Create a line chart
chart = LineChart()
chart.title = "Sales and Profit Before Tax"
chart.style = 10
chart.y_axis.title = "Amount"
chart.x_axis.title = "Week"
chart.legend.position = "b"  # bottom position

# Number of data rows (excluding header)
num_rows = len(df)

# Add Sales data series (column B, rows 1 to num_rows+1 including header)
sales_data = Reference(ws, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_row=num_rows + 1)
chart.add_data(sales_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Add Profit Before Tax data series (column D, rows 1 to num_rows+1 including header)
profit_data = Reference(ws, min_col=4, min_row=1, max_row=num_rows + 1)
chart.add_data(profit_data, titles_from_data=True)

# Set categories (Week column, rows 2 to num_rows+1, excluding header)
categories = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=num_rows + 1)
chart.set_categories(categories)

# Add chart to worksheet starting at cell G2
ws.add_chart(chart, "G2")

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import openpyxl
from datetime import datetime

# Load the workbook
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Work on Sheet1
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Insert a new column after column A (at position B, which is index 2)
ws.insert_cols(2)

# Add header "Formatted Date" in cell B1
ws['B1'] = 'Formatted Date'

# Iterate through rows starting from row 2 (skip header)
for row in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
    date_cell = ws.cell(row=row, column=1)  # Column A
    date_value = date_cell.value
    
    if date_value is not None:
        # Handle datetime or date objects
        if isinstance(date_value, datetime):
            formatted = date_value.strftime('%m-%Y')
        elif isinstance(date_value, str):
            # Try to parse string date
            try:
                # Handle format like '2020-09-16 00:00:00'
                dt = datetime.strptime(date_value.split()[0], '%Y-%m-%d')
                formatted = dt.strftime('%m-%Y')
            except:
                formatted = str(date_value)
        else:
            formatted = str(date_value)
    else:
        formatted = ''
    
    # Write formatted date to column B
    ws.cell(row=row, column=2).value = formatted

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import ScatterChart, Reference, Series

# Load the workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Get the source data sheet
source_sheet = wb['Sheet1']

# Create a new sheet for the chart
chart_sheet = wb.create_sheet(title='Chart')

# Create a scatter chart
chart = ScatterChart()
chart.title = "Range vs. Angle"
chart.style = 13

# Set axis titles
chart.x_axis.title = "Angle"
chart.y_axis.title = "Range"

# Remove legend
chart.legend = None

# Find the last row with data
max_row = source_sheet.max_row

# Create references for X and Y data
# X values: Angle (column A=1, rows 2 to max_row, skipping header)
# Y values: Range (column B=2, rows 2 to max_row, skipping header)
x_values = Reference(source_sheet, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=max_row)
y_values = Reference(source_sheet, min_col=2, min_row=2, max_row=max_row)

# Create and add the series (y values, x values)
series = Series(values=y_values, xvalues=x_values)
chart.series.append(series)

# Add the chart to the new sheet at cell A1
chart_sheet.add_chart(chart, "A1")

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import ScatterChart, Reference, Series

# Load the workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Get the source sheet
source_sheet = wb['Sheet1']

# Create a new sheet for the chart
chart_sheet = wb.create_sheet(title='Chart')

# Create a scatter chart
chart = ScatterChart()
chart.title = "Range vs. Angle"
chart.style = 10

# Set X-axis title
chart.x_axis.title = "Angle"
# Set Y-axis title
chart.y_axis.title = "Range"

# Remove legend
chart.legend = None

# Define the data range for X-axis (Angle - column A, rows 2 to 38)
x_values = Reference(source_sheet, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=38)
# Define the data range for Y-axis (Range - column B, rows 2 to 38)
y_values = Reference(source_sheet, min_col=2, min_row=2, max_row=38)

# Create series with y-values and x-values
series = Series(values=y_values, xvalues=x_values)
chart.series.append(series)

# Add the chart to the new sheet
chart_sheet.add_chart(chart, "A1")

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import Workbook

# Read the Excel file
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Ensure Milwaukee column is numeric for comparison
df['Milwaukee'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Milwaukee'], errors='coerce')

# Filter rows where Milwaukee distance is less than 2000 miles
filtered_df = df[df['Milwaukee'] < 2000].copy()

# Write to output.xlsx using openpyxl
wb = Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = 'Sheet1'

# Write headers
for col_idx, col_name in enumerate(filtered_df.columns, 1):
    ws.cell(row=1, column=col_idx, value=col_name)

# Write data rows
for row_idx, row in enumerate(filtered_df.values, 2):
    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws.cell(row=row_idx, column=col_idx, value=value)

# Save the output file
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook, Workbook

# Load the original workbook to get all sheet names
original_wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
sheet_names = original_wb.sheetnames

# Read Sheet1 with pandas for easy filtering
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Filter rows where Milwaukee distance is less than 2000 miles
filtered_df = df[df['Milwaukee'] < 2000]

# Create new workbook for output
output_wb = Workbook()

# Remove default sheet created by Workbook()
if 'Sheet' in output_wb.sheetnames:
    del output_wb['Sheet']

# Process each sheet from original workbook
for sheet_name in sheet_names:
    if sheet_name == 'Sheet1':
        # Create filtered Sheet1
        ws = output_wb.create_sheet(title=sheet_name)
        
        # Write headers
        headers = list(filtered_df.columns)
        for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers, 1):
            ws.cell(row=1, column=col_idx, value=header)
        
        # Write data rows
        for row_idx, row in enumerate(filtered_df.values, 2):
            for col_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
                ws.cell(row=row_idx, column=col_idx, value=value)
    else:
        # Copy other sheets as-is
        original_ws = original_wb[sheet_name]
        new_ws = output_wb.create_sheet(title=sheet_name)
        for row in original_ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
            new_ws.append(row)

# Move Sheet1 to be the first sheet if it exists
if 'Sheet1' in output_wb.sheetnames:
    output_wb.move_sheet('Sheet1', offset=-len(output_wb.sheetnames) + 1)

# Save the output workbook
output_wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import openpyxl

# Load the workbook
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Get the source sheet
source_sheet = wb['Sheet1']

# Create a new sheet for the selected customers
new_sheet = wb.create_sheet(title='Selected Customers')

# Define the customers we want to copy
target_customers = ['Berkeley', 'Denver', 'Kansas City', 'Chicago']

# Read all data from source sheet
all_rows = []
for row in source_sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True):
    all_rows.append(row)

# First row is headers
headers = all_rows[0]

# Write headers to new sheet
for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers, start=1):
    new_sheet.cell(row=1, column=col_idx, value=header)

# Find and copy the target customer rows
target_customers_lower = [c.lower() for c in target_customers]
current_row = 2

for row_data in all_rows[1:]:  # Skip header
    customer_name = row_data[0]
    if customer_name and customer_name.lower() in target_customers_lower:
        for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data, start=1):
            new_sheet.cell(row=current_row, column=col_idx, value=value)
        current_row += 1

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils.dataframe import dataframe_to_rows

# Read the input workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Read Sheet1 into pandas for filtering and sorting
df_sheet1 = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Read Sheet2 (chosen countries) - keep it for reference
df_sheet2 = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet2')

# Filter for "Exports of goods and services" indicator
exports_df = df_sheet1[df_sheet1['IndicatorName'] == 'Exports of goods and services'].copy()

# Sort by the most recent year column (2005) in descending order
# Convert to numeric for proper sorting
year_cols = [col for col in exports_df.columns if col.isdigit()]
if year_cols:
    latest_year = max(year_cols)
    exports_df[latest_year] = pd.to_numeric(exports_df[latest_year], errors='coerce')
    exports_df = exports_df.sort_values(by=latest_year, ascending=False)

# Create output workbook
output_wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Remove existing Sheet1 and Sheet2 if they exist, then add filtered data
if 'Sheet1' in output_wb.sheetnames:
    del output_wb['Sheet1']
if 'Sheet2' in output_wb.sheetnames:
    del output_wb['Sheet2']

# Create new Sheet1 with filtered and sorted exports data
ws1 = output_wb.create_sheet('Sheet1')
for r_idx, row in enumerate(dataframe_to_rows(exports_df, index=False, header=True), 1):
    for c_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws1.cell(row=r_idx, column=c_idx, value=value)

for r_idx, row in enumerate(dataframe_to_rows(df_sheet2, index=False, header=True), 1):

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook

# Read the Excel file
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Sort by IndicatorName column in ascending order (A to Z)
df_sorted = df.sort_values(by='IndicatorName', ascending=True)

# Load the workbook to preserve other sheets and structure
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Remove existing Sheet1 if it exists
if 'Sheet1' in wb.sheetnames:
    del wb['Sheet1']

# Create new Sheet1 at position 0
ws = wb.create_sheet('Sheet1', 0)

# Write headers
headers = list(df_sorted.columns)
for col_idx, header in enumerate(headers, 1):
    ws.cell(row=1, column=col_idx, value=header)

# Write data rows
for row_idx, row in enumerate(df_sorted.values, 2):
    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row, 1):
        ws.cell(row=row_idx, column=col_idx, value=value)

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook

# Read the input workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')

# Read the data from Sheet1
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Get the destination columns (all except 'Customers')
destination_cols = ['Seattle', 'Milwaukee', 'Birmingham', 'Oakland']

# Count customers where ALL distances are less than 2000
count = 0
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    # Skip header row if present (first row with 'Customers')
    if idx == 0 and row.get('Customers') == 'Customers':
        continue
    
    # Check if all destination distances are less than 2000
    all_less_than_2000 = True
    for col in destination_cols:
        if col in df.columns:
            try:
                distance = float(row[col])
                if distance >= 2000:
                    all_less_than_2000 = False
                    break
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                all_less_than_2000 = False
                break
    if all_less_than_2000:
        count += 1

# Create new sheet with the count result
if 'Count' in wb.sheetnames:
    del wb['Count']
ws = wb.create_sheet('Count')

# Write header and value
ws['A1'] = 'Count'
ws['A2'] = count

# Save the workbook
wb.save('./output.xlsx')

import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.chart import ScatterChart, Reference

# Read the input workbook
wb = load_workbook('./initial.xlsx')
ws = wb['Sheet1']

# Read data using pandas for calculation
df = pd.read_excel('./initial.xlsx', sheet_name='Sheet1')

# Calculate Future Value
# FV = PV * (1 + r/n)^(t*n)
# where PV = Present Value, r = Annual Interest Rate, n = # Compound Periods, t = Years
df['Future Value'] = df['Present Value'] * (1 + df['Annual Interest Rate'] / df['# Compound Periods']) ** (df['Years'] * df['# Compound Periods'])

# Add header for Future Value in column F
ws.cell(row=1, column=6, value='Future Value')

# Add the calculated values to column F
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    ws.cell(row=idx+2, column=6, value=row['Future Value'])

# Create a new sheet for the chart
chart_sheet = wb.create_sheet(title='Chart')

# Create scatter chart
chart = ScatterChart()
chart.title = "Investment Future Value"
chart.x_axis.title = "No."
chart.y_axis.title = "Future Value"
chart.style = 13

# Define data references for the chart
# X-axis: No. column (column A, rows 2 to last row)
# Y-axis: Future Value column (column F, rows 2 to last row)

xvalues = Reference(ws, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=last_row)
yvalues = Reference(ws, min_col=6, min_row=2, max_row=last_row)

chart.add_series(yvalues, xvalues)

# Add chart to the chart sheet
chart_sheet.add_chart(chart, "A1")
